input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/SLA/legal-violation (9.3) termination rights; no party has a convenience right. Because Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term (with 12-month auto-renewals under 8.2), the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under the playbook. We therefore add a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees (leveraging the existing refund mechanics in Section 10.2) and confirm Vendor has no reciprocal convenience right during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees as new Section 9.4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since the three-year term in Section 8.1 otherwise locks us in with no exit absent Vendor breach. Vendor retains no convenience right during a committed term; if helpful, we can discuss 60 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination fee, or other charge, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during the term of an Order Form.
